summary: Each command's pp:data-source declaration must match what it actually reads: the root pre-run hook enforces it, every command that touches the network declares live or auto, and an auto command handed --data-source local stays offline.
reason: --data-source was only validated against its enum, so the hand-written novel commands accepted any value and served whatever they were coded to fetch: 'anime consistency --data-source local' and 'suggest --data-source local' still hit the network, and 'drift --data-source live' still read local snapshots. Enforcement lives in the root persistent pre-run hook and reads cmd.Annotations[pp:data-source], so a new novel command is covered by declaring its strategy rather than by remembering a per-command call. Enforcement alone is not enough — a declaration that lies is worse than none, so the declarations were corrected too: suggest is live (no local candidate pool), franchise gap is live (its gap list comes from live related-entry pages), track add is auto and skips its optional title fetch under an explicit local, and drift is auto and refuses --record under an explicit local. Commands that genuinely need live data must not claim local.
validated_outcome: go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestDeclaredDataSourceStrategyEnforced|TestDataSourceRejectionEndToEnd|TestLocalDeclaredCommandsDeclareTheSourceTheyActuallyUse|TestWeekLocalOnlyDoesNotFetchLive' walks every annotation, rejects the wrong source end to end, and proves franchise gap refuses local, track add stays offline under local, and drift --record refuses local.
